lessons.body:
**Lesson 255: Revelation: letters to the churches — first love, and lukewarm no more**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we saw the risen Christ among the lampstands. Today he speaks to the churches. To the church in Ephesus he says he knows their deeds, their hard work, and their perseverance. They have tested false apostles and have not grown weary. Yet he holds this against them: You have forsaken the love you had at first. He calls them to remember, repent, and do the things they did at first. Love is not a decoration on top of endurance. It is what endurance is for.

To the church in Smyrna he says he knows their afflictions and their poverty—yet they are rich. He tells them, Do not be afraid of what you are about to suffer. Some will be put in prison and tested. Be faithful, even to the point of death, and I will give you life as your victor’s crown. We hear the prison and the call to be faithful with care, not as a scene to dramatize. Then he speaks to Laodicea, the lukewarm church that says, ‘I am rich; I have acquired wealth and do not need a thing.’ They do not realize they are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked. Because they are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—he is about to spit them out of his mouth. Yet the rebuke is love: Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline. So be earnest and repent. Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me. We leave those words inside the letter and do not close the speech early. The Amen, the faithful and true witness, has not given up on a lukewarm church.

In *Good and Evil in the Churches of Asia and Bethlehem*, on Revelation 2:1–3:22, John Piper takes both the churches’ real good and their real evil seriously, and he will not let a congregation hear only the compliments. In *Things Are Worse Than and Better Than They Seem*, on Revelation 2:8–11, he lingers over Smyrna: the church looks poor and pressed, and Christ says they are rich, and he calls them to be faithful even to the point of death. In *How to Buy Gold When You're Broke*, on Revelation 3:14–22, he takes Laodicea’s boast of wealth and shows how Christ offers what they do not know they need, and how he stands at the door and knocks. The BibleProject guide to Revelation helps us hear the seven letters as one word from the Lord who walks among the lampstands.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Revelation 2:4 has, But I have this against you, that you have left your first love. Revelation 2:10 has, Be faithful until death, and I will give you the crown of life. And Revelation 3:20 has, Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in to him and will dine with him, and he with Me.

The Lord who holds the churches tells the truth about first love lost, about hidden riches in affliction, and about lukewarm wealth that is really poverty. He rebukes because he loves. He knocks because he still wants fellowship.

**Revelation 2:1–11 (NIV)**
1 “To the angel of the church in Ephesus write: These are the words of him who holds the seven stars in his right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands. 2 I know your deeds, your hard work and your perseverance. I know that you cannot tolerate wicked people, that you have tested those who claim to be apostles but are not, and have found them false. 3 You have persevered and have endured hardships for my name, and have not grown weary. 4 Yet I hold this against you: You have forsaken the love you had at first. 5 Consider how far you have fallen! Repent and do the things you did at first. If you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place. 6 But you have this in your favor: You hate the practices of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate. 7 Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To the one who is victorious, I will give the right to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God. 8 “To the angel of the church in Smyrna write: These are the words of him who is the First and the Last, who died and came to life again. 9 I know your afflictions and your poverty—yet you are rich! I know about the slander of those who say they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan. 10 Do not be afraid of what you are about to suffer. I tell you, the devil will put some of you in prison to test you, and you will suffer persecution for ten days. Be faithful, even to the point of death, and I will give you life as your victor’s crown. 11 Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches. The one who is victorious will not be hurt at all by the second death.

**Revelation 3:14–22 (NIV)**
14 “To the angel of the church in Laodicea write: These are the words of the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the ruler of God’s creation. 15 I know your deeds, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were either one or the other! 16 So, because you are lukewarm—neither hot nor cold—I am about to spit you out of my mouth. 17 You say, ‘I am rich; I have acquired wealth and do not need a thing.’ But you do not realize that you are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind and naked. 18 I counsel you to buy from me gold refined in the fire, so you can become rich; and white clothes to wear, so you can cover your shameful nakedness; and salve to put on your eyes, so you can see. 19 Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline. So be earnest and repent. 20 Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me. 21 To the one who is victorious, I will give the right to sit with me on my throne, just as I was victorious and sat down with my Father on his throne. 22 Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has first love grown thin, or where have you called yourself rich and in need of nothing? What would it look like today to repent, to be faithful, and to open the door to the one who knocks?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 256: Revelation: the Lamb who was slain is worthy**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday the risen Christ spoke to his churches about first love and about lukewarm wealth. Today John is shown a scroll in the right hand of him who sits on the throne, sealed with seven seals. A mighty angel proclaims in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?” No one in heaven or on earth or under the earth can open it or even look inside it. John weeps and weeps. Then one of the elders says, “Do not weep! See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed. He is able to open the scroll and its seven seals.”

Then John sees a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain, standing at the center of the throne. The worth of the Lion is the worth of the Lamb who was slain. The living creatures and the elders fall down before him and sing a new song: he is worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, because he was slain, and with his blood he purchased for God persons from every tribe and language and people and nation. We speak of the blood of the Lamb with reverence, not as a spectacle. He has made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign on the earth. Then many angels, thousands upon thousands, and ten thousand times ten thousand, say in a loud voice, “Worthy is the Lamb, who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and praise!” Every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and on the sea sings, “To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise and honor and glory and power, for ever and ever!” And the elders fall down and worship.

In *Christ: The Lion and the Lamb*, on Revelation 5:1–10, John Piper holds those two names together: the Lion of Judah who can open the scroll is the Lamb who was slain. In *Every Race to Reign and Worship*, on Revelation 5:8–14, he lingers over the new song, that the Lamb has purchased people from every tribe and language and people and nation, and that they are made a kingdom and priests. The BibleProject guide to Revelation helps us see this throne-room scene as the center of the book’s hope: history opens in the hands of the slain and risen Lamb.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Revelation 5:5 has, “Stop crying! Behold, the Lion that is from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has overcome so as to open the scroll and its seven seals.” And Revelation 5:12 has, “Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and blessing.”

No one else was worthy. The Lion has triumphed by being the Lamb who was slain. The scroll is in his hands, and the nations are in his purchase. Worthy is the Lamb.

**Revelation 5:1–14 (NIV)**
1 Then I saw in the right hand of him who sat on the throne a scroll with writing on both sides and sealed with seven seals. 2 And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice, “Who is worthy to break the seals and open the scroll?” 3 But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth could open the scroll or even look inside it. 4 I wept and wept because no one was found who was worthy to open the scroll or look inside. 5 Then one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep! See, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed. He is able to open the scroll and its seven seals.” 6 Then I saw a Lamb, looking as if it had been slain, standing at the center of the throne, encircled by the four living creatures and the elders. The Lamb had seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God sent out into all the earth. 7 He went and took the scroll from the right hand of him who sat on the throne. 8 And when he had taken it, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each one had a harp and they were holding golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of God’s people. 9 And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to take the scroll and to open its seals, because you were slain, and with your blood you purchased for God persons from every tribe and language and people and nation. 10 You have made them to be a kingdom and priests to serve our God, and they will reign on the earth.” 11 Then I looked and heard the voice of many angels, numbering thousands upon thousands, and ten thousand times ten thousand. They encircled the throne and the living creatures and the elders. 12 In a loud voice they were saying: “Worthy is the Lamb, who was slain, to receive power and wealth and wisdom and strength and honor and glory and praise!” 13 Then I heard every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and on the sea, and all that is in them, saying: “To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be praise and honor and glory and power, for ever and ever!” 14 The four living creatures said, “Amen,” and the elders fell down and worshiped.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where have you been looking for a lion who will not also be the Lamb? What would it look like today to trust the one who was slain, and to praise him with the people he has purchased from every nation?

lessons.title: Revelation: a multitude no one can count, and the accuser thrown down
lessons.body:
**Lesson 257: Revelation: a multitude no one can count, and the accuser thrown down**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday the Lamb who was slain was found worthy to open the scroll, and he had purchased people from every nation. Today John sees that purchase made visible. After this he looks, and there before him is a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, tribe, people and language, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They are wearing white robes and holding palm branches, and they cry out in a loud voice, “Salvation belongs to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb.” All the angels, the elders, and the four living creatures fall down and worship, saying, “Amen! Praise and glory and wisdom and thanks and honor and power and strength be to our God for ever and ever. Amen!”

One of the elders asks, “These in white robes—who are they, and where did they come from?” John answers, “Sir, you know.” And the elder says that these are they who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Therefore they are before the throne of God and serve him day and night in his temple, and he who sits on the throne will shelter them with his presence. Never again will they hunger; never again will they thirst. The Lamb at the center of the throne will be their shepherd; ‘he will lead them to springs of living water.’ ‘And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.’ We hear the blood and the tribulation with dignity, not as a spectacle and not as a cartoon.

lessons.title: Revelation: the wedding of the Lamb, and the King of kings
lessons.body:
**Lesson 258: Revelation: the wedding of the Lamb, and the King of kings**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we saw a multitude no one could count, and the accuser thrown down. Today heaven sounds like a great multitude shouting that salvation and glory and power belong to our God, for true and just are his judgments. The text then speaks of God’s judgment on a great corrupt power, in the language of a prostitute and of adulteries. We say that simply, with dignity, and we do not turn judgment into a spectacle. Again they shout, “Hallelujah! The smoke from her goes up for ever and ever.” The elders and the living creatures fall down and cry, “Amen, Hallelujah!” A voice from the throne says, “Praise our God, all you his servants, you who fear him, both great and small!”

Then John hears what sounds like a great multitude, like the roar of rushing waters and like loud peals of thunder, shouting, Hallelujah! For our Lord God Almighty reigns. Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready. Fine linen, bright and clean, was given her to wear. (Fine linen stands for the righteous acts of God’s holy people.) The angel says, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb!” And he adds, “These are the true words of God.” John falls at the angel’s feet to worship him, but the angel says, “Don’t do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your brothers and sisters who hold to the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For it is the Spirit of prophecy who bears testimony to Jesus.”

Then John sees heaven standing open, and a white horse, whose rider is called Faithful and True. With justice he judges and wages war. His eyes are like blazing fire, and on his head are many crowns. He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is the Word of God. The armies of heaven follow him, wearing fine linen, white and clean. Coming out of his mouth is a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations. “He will rule them with an iron scepter.” He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty. We tell the sword, the robe, and the winepress with care, not as gore and not as a cartoon. On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: king of kings and lord of lords.

In *Worship God!*, on Revelation 19:1–10, John Piper takes the angel’s correction as the point of the wedding scene: even a holy messenger must not be worshiped. The Hallelujahs, the wedding of the Lamb, and the invitation all drive to this: Worship God! For the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11–16, I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is that second half of the chapter, so we stay with the text itself and with the BibleProject guide to Revelation, which helps us see the Faithful and True rider as the same Jesus who is the Word of God, king of kings and lord of lords.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Revelation 19:9 has, “Write, ‘Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.’” And he *said to me, “These are true words of God.” And Revelation 19:16 has, And He has on His garment and on His thigh a name written, “KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS.”

The wedding of the Lamb is joy, and the rider called Faithful and True is the King who makes that joy safe. Do not worship the messenger. Worship God. The name written on him is king of kings and lord of lords.

**Revelation 19:1–16 (NIV)**
1 After this I heard what sounded like the roar of a great multitude in heaven shouting: “Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God, 2 for true and just are his judgments. He has condemned the great prostitute who corrupted the earth by her adulteries. He has avenged on her the blood of his servants.” 3 And again they shouted: “Hallelujah! The smoke from her goes up for ever and ever.” 4 The twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God, who was seated on the throne. And they cried: “Amen, Hallelujah!” 5 Then a voice came from the throne, saying: “Praise our God, all you his servants, you who fear him, both great and small!” 6 Then I heard what sounded like a great multitude, like the roar of rushing waters and like loud peals of thunder, shouting: “Hallelujah! For our Lord God Almighty reigns. 7 Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready. 8 Fine linen, bright and clean, was given her to wear.” (Fine linen stands for the righteous acts of God’s holy people.) 9 Then the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb!” And he added, “These are the true words of God.” 10 At this I fell at his feet to worship him. But he said to me, “Don’t do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your brothers and sisters who hold to the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For it is the Spirit of prophecy who bears testimony to Jesus.” 11 I saw heaven standing open and there before me was a white horse, whose rider is called Faithful and True. With justice he judges and wages war. 12 His eyes are like blazing fire, and on his head are many crowns. He has a name written on him that no one knows but he himself. 13 He is dressed in a robe dipped in blood, and his name is the Word of God. 14 The armies of heaven were following him, riding on white horses and dressed in fine linen, white and clean. 15 Coming out of his mouth is a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations. “He will rule them with an iron scepter.” He treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty. 16 On his robe and on his thigh he has this name written: king of kings and lord of lords.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, what lesser voice have you been tempted to honor in the place of God, and how does the wedding of the Lamb call you back? What would it look like today to worship God, and to trust the rider who is Faithful and True?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 259: Revelation: the last judgment, and a new heaven and a new earth**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we heard the wedding of the Lamb, and we saw the rider called Faithful and True. Today the book brings us to the last judgment, and then to a new heaven and a new earth. John sees a great white throne and him who was seated on it. The earth and the heavens flee from his presence, and there is no place for them. The dead, great and small, stand before the throne, and books are opened. Another book is opened, which is the book of life. The dead are judged according to what they had done as recorded in the books. The sea, death, and Hades give up the dead in them, and each person is judged according to what they had done. Then death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire. The lake of fire is the second death. Anyone whose name is not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire. We teach this with gravity and with care, not as a scare, and not as a spectacle.

Then I saw “a new heaven and a new earth,” for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea. John sees the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband. A loud voice from the throne says, “Look! God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. ‘He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death’ or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.” He who was seated on the throne said, “I am making everything new!” Then he said, “Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.” He said to me, It is done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the thirsty I will give water without cost from the spring of the water of life. Those who are victorious will inherit all this, and I will be their God and they will be my children. The same speech also tells the truth about those who refuse him: the cowardly, the unbelieving, the vile, the murderers, the sexually immoral, those who practice magic arts, the idolaters and all liars will be consigned to the fiery lake of burning sulfur. This is the second death. We name that list briefly and pastorally, without turning any part of it into a show. The last word over the people of God is not the lake of fire. It is this: God will dwell with them, and he is making everything new.

I looked for a John Piper sermon on Desiring God whose main text is Revelation 20:11–15, and I did not find a /messages/ sermon on that range, so we stay with the text itself and with the BibleProject guide to Revelation for the great white throne. For the new heaven and the new earth, two sermons on Revelation 21:1–8 help us hear the hope: in *Behold, I Make All Things New*, Piper takes the voice from the throne as the heart of the ending, that God himself will dwell with his people and make all things new; in *I Am Alpha and Omega*, he lingers over the one who is the Beginning and the End, who gives the water of life without cost to the thirsty.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Revelation 21:3 has, Behold, the tabernacle of God is among men, and He will dwell among them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself will be among them. Revelation 21:5 has, “Behold, I am making all things new.” And He *said, “Write, for these words are faithful and true.” And Revelation 21:6 has, They are done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. I will give to the one who thirsts from the spring of the water of life without cost.

The books are opened, and so is the book of life. Judgment is real, and it is not a game. Then the first things pass away, and the voice from the throne says, “I am making everything new!” The Alpha and the Omega will dwell with his people, and he will wipe every tear from their eyes.

**Revelation 20:11–15 (NIV)**
11 Then I saw a great white throne and him who was seated on it. The earth and the heavens fled from his presence, and there was no place for them. 12 And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged according to what they had done as recorded in the books. 13 The sea gave up the dead that were in it, and death and Hades gave up the dead that were in them, and each person was judged according to what they had done. 14 Then death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. The lake of fire is the second death. 15 Anyone whose name was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.

**Revelation 21:1–8 (NIV)**
1 Then I saw “a new heaven and a new earth,” for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea. 2 I saw the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband. 3 And I heard a loud voice from the throne saying, “Look! God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. 4 ‘He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death’ or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.” 5 He who was seated on the throne said, “I am making everything new!” Then he said, “Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.” 6 He said to me: “It is done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the thirsty I will give water without cost from the spring of the water of life. 7 Those who are victorious will inherit all this, and I will be their God and they will be my children. 8 But the cowardly, the unbelieving, the vile, the murderers, the sexually immoral, those who practice magic arts, the idolaters and all liars—they will be consigned to the fiery lake of burning sulfur. This is the second death.”

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, how does the book of life, and not only the record of deeds, teach you to hope, and how does “I am making everything new!” teach you to live today? What would it look like to thirst for the water of life, and to walk as someone who will be God’s child in the new creation?

Then death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire. The lake of fire is the second death. Anyone whose name is not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire. We teach this with gravity and with care, not as a scare, and not as a spectacle.

Then I saw “a new heaven and a new earth,” for the first heaven and the first earth had passed away, and there was no longer any sea. God’s dwelling place is now among the people, and he will dwell with them. They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God. ‘He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death’ or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.” He who was seated on the throne said, “I am making everything new!” Then he said, “Write this down, for these words are trustworthy and true.” He said to me, It is done. I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the thirsty I will give water without cost from the spring of the water of life. Those who are victorious will inherit all this, and I will be their God and they will be my children. The same speech also tells the truth about those who refuse him: the cowardly, the unbelieving, the vile, the murderers, the sexually immoral, those who practice magic arts, the idolaters and all liars will be consigned to the fiery lake of burning sulfur. This is the second death. We name that list briefly and pastorally, without turning any part of it into a show. The last word over the people of God is not the lake of fire. It is this: God will dwell with them, and he is making everything new.

I looked for a John Piper sermon on Desiring God whose main text is Revelation 20:11–15, and I did not find a /messages/ sermon on that range, so we stay with the text itself and with the BibleProject guide to Revelation for the great white throne. Another book was opened, which is the book of life. The dead were judged according to what they had done as recorded in the books. 13 The sea gave up the dead that were in it, and death and Hades gave up the dead that were in them, and each person was judged according to what they had done. 14 Then death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire. lessons.body:
**Lesson 260: Revelation: the river of life; yes, I am coming soon**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we stood at the last judgment, and then at a new heaven and a new earth, where God will dwell with his people and make everything new. Today one of the seven angels says, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.” John is carried away in the Spirit to a great, high mountain, and he is shown the Holy City, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God. It shines with the glory of God, like a very precious jewel, clear as crystal. It has twelve gates named for the tribes of Israel, and twelve foundations named for the apostles of the Lamb. The Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. The city does not need the sun or the moon, for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp. The nations will walk by its light. Nothing impure will ever enter it, nor will anyone who does what is shameful or deceitful, but only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life. We hear that last line with gravity, not as a scare.

Then the angel shows him the river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb down the middle of the great street of the city. On each side of the river stands the tree of life, yielding its fruit every month, and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations. No longer will there be any curse. His servants will see his face. When John falls down to worship the angel, the angel says, “Don’t do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your fellow prophets and with all who keep the words of this scroll. Worship God!” The risen Lord says, “Look, I am coming soon! Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy written in this scroll.” The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And let the one who hears say, “Come!” Let the one who is thirsty come; and let the one who wishes take the free gift of the water of life. He who testifies to these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Amen. Come, Lord Jesus. The book ends, The grace of the Lord Jesus be with God’s people. Amen. Where the text names those who remain outside, we say that briefly and with care, and we do not turn it into a spectacle.

I looked for a John Piper sermon on Desiring God whose main text is Revelation 21:9–27, or the river of life and the coming-soon words of Revelation 22, and I did not find a /messages/ sermon on those ranges. In *Worship God*, on Revelation 22:8–9, Piper takes the angel’s correction at the end of the book as seriously as at the wedding scene: even a holy messenger must not be worshiped. Worship God. For the city, the river, and the promise, “Yes, I am coming soon.” we stay with the text itself and with the BibleProject guide to Revelation.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Revelation 21:22 has, And I saw no sanctuary in it, for the Lord God the Almighty and the Lamb are its sanctuary. Revelation 22:7 has, “And behold, I am coming quickly. Blessed is he who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book.” And Revelation 22:20 has, “Yes, I am coming quickly.”

The Bible does not end with a closed door. It ends with a river, a tree, an open invitation, and a promise. The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And the Lord says, “Yes, I am coming soon.”

**Revelation 21:9–27 (NIV)**
9 One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues came and said to me, “Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb.” 10 And he carried me away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high, and showed me the Holy City, Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God. 11 It shone with the glory of God, and its brilliance was like that of a very precious jewel, like a jasper, clear as crystal. 12 It had a great, high wall with twelve gates, and with twelve angels at the gates. On the gates were written the names of the twelve tribes of Israel. 13 There were three gates on the east, three on the north, three on the south and three on the west. 14 The wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb. 15 The angel who talked with me had a measuring rod of gold to measure the city, its gates and its walls. 16 The city was laid out like a square, as long as it was wide. He measured the city with the rod and found it to be 12,000 stadia in length, and as wide and high as it is long. 17 The angel measured the wall using human measurement, and it was 144 cubits thick. 18 The wall was made of jasper, and the city of pure gold, as pure as glass. 19 The foundations of the city walls were decorated with every kind of precious stone. The first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third agate, the fourth emerald, 20 the fifth onyx, the sixth ruby, the seventh chrysolite, the eighth beryl, the ninth topaz, the tenth turquoise, the eleventh jacinth, and the twelfth amethyst. 21 The twelve gates were twelve pearls, each gate made of a single pearl. The great street of the city was of gold, as pure as transparent glass. 22 I did not see a temple in the city, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple. 23 The city does not need the sun or the moon to shine on it, for the glory of God gives it light, and the Lamb is its lamp. 24 The nations will walk by its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their splendor into it. 25 On no day will its gates ever be shut, for there will be no night there. 26 The glory and honor of the nations will be brought into it. 27 Nothing impure will ever enter it, nor will anyone who does what is shameful or deceitful, but only those whose names are written in the Lamb’s book of life.

**Revelation 22:1–21 (NIV)**
1 Then the angel showed me the river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb 2 down the middle of the great street of the city. On each side of the river stood the tree of life, bearing twelve crops of fruit, yielding its fruit every month. And the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations. 3 No longer will there be any curse. The throne of God and of the Lamb will be in the city, and his servants will serve him. 4 They will see his face, and his name will be on their foreheads. 5 There will be no more night. They will not need the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God will give them light. And they will reign for ever and ever. 6 The angel said to me, “These words are trustworthy and true. The Lord, the God who inspires the prophets, sent his angel to show his servants the things that must soon take place.” 7 “Look, I am coming soon! Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy written in this scroll.” 8 I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And when I had heard and seen them, I fell down to worship at the feet of the angel who had been showing them to me. 9 But he said to me, “Don’t do that! I am a fellow servant with you and with your fellow prophets and with all who keep the words of this scroll. Worship God!” 10 Then he told me, “Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this scroll, because the time is near. 11 Let the one who does wrong continue to do wrong; let the vile person continue to be vile; let the one who does right continue to do right; and let the holy person continue to be holy.” 12 “Look, I am coming soon! My reward is with me, and I will give to each person according to what they have done. 13 I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End. 14 “Blessed are those who wash their robes, that they may have the right to the tree of life and may go through the gates into the city. 15 Outside are the dogs, those who practice magic arts, the sexually immoral, the murderers, the idolaters and everyone who loves and practices falsehood. 16 “I, Jesus, have sent my angel to give you this testimony for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, and the bright Morning Star.” 17 The Spirit and the bride say, “Come!” And let the one who hears say, “Come!” Let the one who is thirsty come; and let the one who wishes take the free gift of the water of life. 18 I warn everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this scroll: If anyone adds anything to them, God will add to that person the plagues described in this scroll. 19 And if anyone takes words away from this scroll of prophecy, God will take away from that person any share in the tree of life and in the Holy City, which are described in this scroll. 20 He who testifies to these things says, “Yes, I am coming soon.” Amen. Come, Lord Jesus. 21 The grace of the Lord Jesus be with God’s people. Amen.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has your hope grown thin for the ending God has promised? What would it look like today to say “Come!” with the Spirit and the bride, and to keep the words of this book while you wait for the one who says, “Yes, I am coming soon.”?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 261: Marriage as covenant, not contract**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday the Bible closed with the river of life and the promise, Yes, I am coming soon. Today, as we connect with this week’s Grace Life sermon, we turn to marriage as covenant, not contract. In Malachi the people flood the LORD’s altar with tears, because he no longer looks with favor on their offerings. They ask, “Why?” It is because the LORD is the witness between them and the wife of their youth. They have been unfaithful to her, though she is their partner, the wife of their marriage covenant. Has not the one God made you? You belong to him in body and spirit. And what does the one God seek? Godly offspring. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful to the wife of your youth.

Then the LORD says, “The man who hates and divorces his wife,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “does violence to the one he should protect,” says the LORD Almighty. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful. We teach this with gravity and with care. The text does not treat a wife as disposable, and it names unfaithfulness as a real wound. We do not use these words to shame anyone who has already suffered a broken marriage, and we do not treat them lightly as if covenant were only a feeling that can be dropped. Marriage here is a covenant before God, not a contract you end when it no longer serves you.

Jesus takes us back to the beginning. He replies, “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’ and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” The joining is God’s work. That is why a marriage is more than a private arrangement.

In *Let None Be Faithless to the Wife of His Youth*, on Malachi 2:10–16, John Piper treats marriage as a covenant to which the LORD himself is witness, and he will not let unfaithfulness be renamed as a small thing. In *What God Has Joined Together, Let Not Man Separate, Part 2*, on Matthew 19:3–12, he follows Jesus back to the Creator’s design: God made them male and female, God joins the two as one flesh, and no one is to pull apart what God has joined. The BibleProject guides to Malachi and Matthew help us keep both texts in their larger story: a people being called back to covenant faithfulness, and a Lord who restores marriage to the way it was at the beginning.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Malachi 2:14 has, Because Yahweh has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant. And Matthew 19:6 has, What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.

The LORD is witness to the marriage covenant. The wife of your youth is a partner, not a possession to discard. What God has joined together, let no one separate.

**Malachi 2:13–16 (NIV)**
13 Another thing you do: You flood the LORD’s altar with tears. You weep and wail because he no longer looks with favor on your offerings or accepts them with pleasure from your hands. 14 You ask, “Why?” It is because the LORD is the witness between you and the wife of your youth. You have been unfaithful to her, though she is your partner, the wife of your marriage covenant. 15 Has not the one God made you? You belong to him in body and spirit. And what does the one God seek? Godly offspring. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful to the wife of your youth. 16 “The man who hates and divorces his wife,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “does violence to the one he should protect,” says the LORD Almighty. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful.

**Matthew 19:4–6 (NIV)**
4 “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’ 5 and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? 6 So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where have you been tempted to treat covenant like a contract, or to grow careless with the one God joined you to? What would it look like today to be on your guard, to be faithful, and to honor what God has joined together?

In *Let None Be Faithless to the Wife of His Youth*, on Malachi 2:10–16, John Piper treats marriage as a covenant to which the LORD himself is witness, and he will not let unfaithfulness be renamed as a small thing. In *What God Has Joined Together, Let Not Man Separate, Part 2*, on Matthew 19:3–12, he follows Jesus back to the Creator’s design: God made them male and female, God joins the two as one flesh, and no one is to pull apart what God has joined. The BibleProject guides to Malachi and Matthew help us keep both texts in their larger story: a people being called back to covenant faithfulness, and a Lord who restores marriage to the way it was at the beginning.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Malachi 2:14 has, Because Yahweh has been a witness between you and the wife of your youth, against whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and your wife by covenant. And Matthew 19:6 has, What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.

The LORD is witness to the marriage covenant. The wife of your youth is a partner, not a possession to discard. What God has joined together, let no one separate.

13 Another thing you do: You flood the LORD’s altar with tears. You weep and wail because he no longer looks with favor on your offerings or accepts them with pleasure from your hands. 14 You ask, “Why?” It is because the LORD is the witness between you and the wife of your youth. You have been unfaithful to her, though she is your partner, the wife of your marriage covenant. 15 Has not the one God made you? You belong to him in body and spirit. And what does the one God seek? Godly offspring. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful to the wife of your youth. 16 “The man who hates and divorces his wife,” says the LORD, the God of Israel, “does violence to the one he should protect,” says the LORD Almighty. So be on your guard, and do not be unfaithful.

**Matthew 19:4–6 (NIV)**
4 “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’ 5 and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? 6 So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”

**For reflection.** As a woman, wife, and a mother, where have you been tempted to treat covenant like a contract, or to grow careless with the one God joined you to? What would it look like today to be on your guard, to be faithful, and to honor what God has joined together?

lessons.title: The design of marriage: one flesh

sources.label: John Piper, Staying Married Is Not About Staying in Love (Desiring God)

lessons.body:
**Lesson 262: The design of marriage: one flesh**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we heard that marriage is a covenant to which the LORD is witness, and that what God has joined together, no one is to separate. Today we go back to the design itself. The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.” Helper here is not a lesser word. It is God’s own gift of a counterpart fit for the man. The LORD brings the animals to the man, and the man names them, but for Adam no suitable helper is found. Then the LORD God causes the man to fall into a deep sleep, takes one of the man’s ribs, and makes a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brings her to the man.

The man said, “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for she was taken out of man.” That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh. Adam and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame. We say that last line simply, with dignity. It is not a joke, and it is not a scene to linger on. In the design God gave, the man and the woman could stand before one another without fear. One flesh is God’s joining: shared life, shared belonging, a union he himself made.

In *Staying Married Is Not About Staying in Love*, on Genesis 2:18–25, John Piper traces the design as God’s doing: God sees that it is not good for the man to be alone, God makes a suitable helper, God brings her to the man, and God speaks the one-flesh union into the world. Marriage is not first a mood we keep trying to feel. It is a design we receive. The BibleProject guide to Genesis helps us hear this scene in the larger gift of creation, before the later wound of the fall.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Genesis 2:18 has, “It is not good for the man to be alone; I will make him a helper suitable for him.” And Genesis 2:24 has, Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife; and they shall become one flesh.

The man was not made to be alone, and the woman is not an afterthought. She is a suitable helper, bone of his bones, and the two become one flesh. That is the design.

**Genesis 2:18–25 (NIV)**
18 The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.” 19 Now the LORD God had formed out of the ground all the wild animals and all the birds in the sky. He brought them to the man to see what he would name them; and whatever the man called each living creature, that was its name. 20 So the man gave names to all the livestock, the birds in the sky and all the wild animals. But for Adam no suitable helper was found. 21 So the LORD God caused the man to fall into a deep sleep; and while he was sleeping, he took one of the man’s ribs and then closed up the place with flesh. 22 Then the LORD God made a woman from the rib he had taken out of the man, and he brought her to the man. 23 The man said, “This is now bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called ‘woman,’ for she was taken out of man.” 24 That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh. 25 Adam and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, how does this first gift of a suitable helper, and of one flesh, correct a small or selfish view of marriage? What would it look like today to receive your marriage, or to honor marriage itself, as God’s design rather than as a private invention?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 263: Leaving and cleaving**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we watched God make a suitable helper and bring her to the man, and we heard that the two become one flesh. Today the text names the movement that union requires. That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh. Leaving is not a cruelty to father and mother. It is the honest start of a new household. Cleaving, being united, is not a mood. It is a holding fast to the wife God has given.

Jesus reads that design as the Creator’s own word. He says, “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’ and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.” The leaving and the uniting are not only Adam’s story. They are the reason a marriage may not be pulled apart as if it were only two people deciding for themselves. God has joined them. We hear that with honor, and with care for anyone who already knows the grief of a breaking.

In *Staying Married Is Not About Staying in Love*, on Genesis 2:18–25, John Piper lingers over this leaving and holding fast as God’s spoken design, not a later human custom. In *What God Has Joined Together, Let Not Man Separate, Part 2*, on Matthew 19:3–12, he follows Jesus as Jesus puts Genesis 2:24 in the Creator’s mouth: the one who made them male and female also said that the two will become one flesh. The BibleProject guides to Genesis and Matthew help us hear the same design at the beginning and in the mouth of Jesus.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Genesis 2:24 has, Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife; and they shall become one flesh. And Matthew 19:5 has, ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh’?

Leave. Be united. Become one flesh. What God has joined together, let no one separate.

**Genesis 2:24 (NIV)**
24 That is why a man leaves his father and mother and is united to his wife, and they become one flesh.

**Matthew 19:4–6 (NIV)**
4 “Haven’t you read,” he replied, “that at the beginning the Creator ‘made them male and female,’ 5 and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’? 6 So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.”

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where is leaving still unfinished, or uniting still thin, in the household God has given you? What would it look like today to hold fast, and to treat your union as something God has joined?

lessons.title: A husband's duty: love her as Christ loved the church

sources.label: John Piper, Husbands Who Love Like Christ and the Wives Who Submit to Them (Desiring God)

lessons.body:
**Lesson 264: A husband's duty: love her as Christ loved the church**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday Jesus took us back to leaving and being united, and to the one flesh God joins. Today the husband’s duty is named in the light of Christ. Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her to make her holy, cleansing her by the washing with water through the word, and to present her to himself as a radiant church, without stain or wrinkle or any other blemish, but holy and blameless. The measure is not a husband’s preference. The measure is a Savior who gave himself up.

In this same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. After all, no one ever hated their own body, but they feed and care for their body, just as Christ does the church—for we are members of his body. Then the profound mystery is named with the older words, “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.” Paul says he is talking about Christ and the church. However, each one of you also must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband. We teach the husband’s call without swagger and without excuse. Headship, when the next verses are read with this one, is not a right to command and control. It is a responsibility to love like Christ: to give yourself up, to nourish, to cherish, to seek her good.

In *Husbands Who Love Like Christ and the Wives Who Submit to Them*, on Ephesians 5:21–33, John Piper will not let headship be turned into domination, or love be reduced to a feeling. The husband is to key off the way Christ loves the church. In *Marriage: Pursuing Conformity to Christ in the Covenant*, also on Ephesians 5:21–33, he lingers over the husband’s costly aim: not to remake a wife in his own image, but to love her toward holiness as Christ loves his people. The official range today is Ephesians 5:25–33; we stay with that calling and do not use the text to excuse harshness. The BibleProject guide to Ephesians helps us hear this household word inside the larger letter about life in Christ.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Ephesians 5:25 has, Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself up for her. And Ephesians 5:33 has, Nevertheless, each individual among you also is to love his own wife even as himself, and the wife must see to it that she respects her husband.

The husband does not get a smaller law than the cross. Love her as Christ loved the church. Give yourself up. Feed and care. Love her as you love yourself.

**Ephesians 5:25–33 (NIV)**
25 Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her 26 to make her holy, cleansing her by the washing with water through the word, 27 and to present her to himself as a radiant church, without stain or wrinkle or any other blemish, but holy and blameless. 28 In this same way, husbands ought to love their wives as their own bodies. He who loves his wife loves himself. 29 After all, no one ever hated their own body, but they feed and care for their body, just as Christ does the church— 30 for we are members of his body. 31 “For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be united to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.” 32 This is a profound mystery—but I am talking about Christ and the church. 33 However, each one of you also must love his wife as he loves himself, and the wife must respect her husband.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has love grown cheap, self-protecting, or demanding? What would it look like today to give yourself up as Christ did, and to nourish and cherish the one you have been given?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 265: A husband's duty: live with her according to knowledge**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday the husband was called to love his wife as Christ loved the church and gave himself up for her. Today that love is given a close, ordinary shape. Husbands, in the same way be considerate as you live with your wives, and treat them with respect as the weaker partner and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life, so that nothing will hinder your prayers. We handle weaker partner with care. The text does not mean a lesser person, or a lesser heir. She is an heir with you of the gracious gift of life. Respect is the command. Understanding is the way you live with her. And God ties this so closely to a husband’s life with him that unkindness can hinder his prayers.

Colossians says the same duty in a short, sharp line: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them. Harshness is not a small fault the text shrugs at. Love and harshness cannot share the same house in peace. The husband who will not be considerate, who will not honor his wife as a fellow heir, should not expect a free and open life of prayer. This is not a call to fuss over a wife as if she were fragile in dignity. It is a call to honor, knowledge, and a refused harshness. We say that plainly, and we do not turn any part of it into a joke.

In *That Your Prayers May Not Be Hindered*, on 1 Peter 3:7, John Piper takes the last clause seriously: there is a way of living with a wife that clogs a husband’s prayers, and a way of understanding, honor, and shared heirship that helps them. In *Honor, Guard, and Cherish*, and in *Men, Love and Lead Your Wives*, also on 1 Peter 3:7, he keeps returning to that same verse: live with her according to knowledge, show honor, remember that she is a fellow heir of the grace of life. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Colossians 3:19, so that short word is taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Colossians: love your wives, and do not be harsh with them. The BibleProject guide to 1 Peter helps us hear the honor of the verse as well.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: 1 Peter 3:7 has, You husbands in the same way, live with your wives in an understanding way, as with a weaker vessel, since she is a woman; and show her honor as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered. And Colossians 3:19 has, Husbands, love your wives and do not be embittered against them.

Be considerate. Show honor. Remember she is a fellow heir. Love her, and do not be harsh. A husband’s prayers are not separate from the way he lives with his wife.

**1 Peter 3:7 (NIV)**
7 Husbands, in the same way be considerate as you live with your wives, and treat them with respect as the weaker partner and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life, so that nothing will hinder your prayers.

**Colossians 3:19 (NIV)**
19 Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has harshness, hurry, or a failure to understand crept into the way you share a house? What would it look like today to live with honor, as with a fellow heir of the gracious gift of life, so that prayer is not hindered?

We handle weaker partner with care. The text does not mean a lesser person, or a lesser heir. She is an heir with you of the gracious gift of life. Respect is the command. Understanding is the way you live with her. And God ties this so closely to a husband’s life with him that unkindness can hinder his prayers.

Colossians says the same duty in a short, sharp line: Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them. Harshness is not a small fault the text shrugs at. Love and harshness cannot share the same house in peace. The husband who will not be considerate, who will not honor his wife as a fellow heir, should not expect a free and open life of prayer. This is not a call to fuss over a wife as if she were fragile in dignity. It is a call to honor, knowledge, and a refused harshness. We say that plainly, and we do not turn any part of it into a joke.

In *That Your Prayers May Not Be Hindered*, on 1 Peter 3:7, John Piper takes the last clause seriously: there is a way of living with a wife that clogs a husband’s prayers, and a way of understanding, honor, and shared heirship that helps them. In *Honor, Guard, and Cherish*, and in *Men, Love and Lead Your Wives*, also on 1 Peter 3:7, he keeps returning to that same verse: live with her according to knowledge, show honor, remember that she is a fellow heir of the grace of life. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Colossians 3:19, so that short word is taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Colossians: love your wives, and do not be harsh with them. The BibleProject guide to 1 Peter helps us hear the honor of the verse as well.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: 1 Peter 3:7 has, You husbands in the same way, live with your wives in an understanding way, as with a weaker vessel, since she is a woman; and show her honor as a fellow heir of the grace of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered. And Colossians 3:19 has, Husbands, love your wives and do not be embittered against them.

Be considerate. Show honor. Remember she is a fellow heir. Love her, and do not be harsh. A husband’s prayers are not separate from the way he lives with his wife.

**1 Peter 3:7 (NIV)**
7 Husbands, in the same way be considerate as you live with your wives, and treat them with respect as the weaker partner and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life, so that nothing will hinder your prayers.

**Colossians 3:19 (NIV)**
19 Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh with them.

**For reflection.** As a woman, wife, and a mother, where has harshness, hurry, or a failure to understand crept into the way you share a house? What would it look like today to live with honor, as with a fellow heir of the gracious gift of life, so that prayer is not hindered?

lessons.body:
**Lesson 266: A wife's honor, help, and holy strength**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday the husband was told to live with his wife according to knowledge, and not to be harsh. Today the text honors a wife’s strength. A wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies. Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value. She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life. This is not a soft ornament. Noble character is holy strength: trusted, valuable, and a source of good.

Paul writes, Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as you do to the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the church, his body, of which he is the Savior. Now as the church submits to Christ, so also wives should submit to their husbands in everything. We teach this with dignity, not as cowering, and not as a blank check for a husband’s sin. The pattern is the church’s glad relation to Christ the Savior, not fear of a harsh man. And the first design still stands: The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.” Helper is not a demotion. In this story it is the gift that answers what was not good, a counterpart fit for the man, strong enough to stand with him. Honor, help, and holy strength belong together.

In *Husbands Who Love Like Christ and the Wives Who Submit to Them*, on Ephesians 5:21–33, John Piper will not let submission be turned into coerced smallness. The wife keys off the church’s relation to Christ, and the husband’s headship is answerable to the cross. In *Staying Married Is Not About Staying in Love*, on Genesis 2:18–25, he treats the suitable helper as God’s own completing gift, not as an afterthought. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Proverbs 31:10–12, so that portrait is taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Proverbs: a wife of noble character, trusted, bringing good all the days of her life. The BibleProject guide to Ephesians helps us keep the household call inside the gospel of Christ and the church.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Proverbs 31:10–11 has, An excellent wife, who can find? For her worth is far above pearls. The heart of her husband trusts in her, And he will have no lack of gain. And Ephesians 5:22 has, Wives, be subject to your own husbands, as to the Lord.

She is worth far more than rubies. She is a suitable helper, not a lesser person. Her honor and her strength are holy, and her yes to her husband is patterned on the church’s yes to Christ.

**Proverbs 31:10–12 (NIV)**
10 A wife of noble character who can find? She is worth far more than rubies. 11 Her husband has full confidence in her and lacks nothing of value. 12 She brings him good, not harm, all the days of her life.

**Ephesians 5:22–24 (NIV)**
22 Wives, submit yourselves to your own husbands as you do to the Lord. 23 For the husband is the head of the wife as Christ is the head of the church, his body, of which he is the Savior. 24 Now as the church submits to Christ, so also wives should submit to their husbands in everything.

**Genesis 2:18 (NIV)**
18 The LORD God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make a helper suitable for him.”

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, how have you pictured a wife’s honor—as thin usefulness, or as noble character and holy strength? What would it look like today to honor that gift, to bring good, and to walk in a glad, dignified relation to the Lord?

lessons.title: Mutual honor: submit to one another out of reverence for Christ

sources.label: John Piper, Husbands Who Love Like Christ and the Wives Who Submit to Them (Desiring God)

John Piper, The Mind of Christ: Looking Out for the Interests of Others (Desiring God)

lessons.body:
**Lesson 267: Mutual honor: submit to one another out of reverence for Christ**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we honored a wife’s noble character, her suitable help, and her holy strength. Today the house is given a shared word: Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ. Mutual honor is not a contest, and it is not the erasing of every difference. It is a holy stooping, because Christ is worthy of reverence. We come to one another, in the home, not first to be served but to honor.

Philippians shows the same mind. If there is any encouragement from being united with Christ, any comfort from his love, any common sharing in the Spirit, any tenderness and compassion, then be like-minded, having the same love, being one in spirit and of one mind. Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others. In your relationships with one another, have the same mindset as Christ Jesus. The verse ends there, with a colon, and the letter then turns our eyes to Christ’s own humility. We do not take up those next verses as today’s official text. We do take the call: this mindset, in this house, toward this person.

In *Husbands Who Love Like Christ and the Wives Who Submit to Them*, and in *Jesus Is Precious as the Foundation of the Family*, John Piper treats Ephesians 5:21 as Spirit-grown honor: we submit to one another out of reverence for Christ, and that mutual honor does not cancel the later callings in the household, but transforms them. In *The Mind of Christ: Looking Out for the Interests of Others*, on Philippians 2, he lingers over the humility that values others and looks to their interests, the mindset we are to have as Christ Jesus. The BibleProject guides to Ephesians and Philippians help us hear both texts as the gospel’s ordinary posture, not as a tool for winning an argument at home.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Ephesians 5:21 has, and being subject to one another in the fear of Christ. Philippians 2:3 has, doing nothing from selfish ambition or vain glory, but with humility of mind regarding one another as more important than yourselves. And Philippians 2:5 has, Have this way of thinking in yourselves which was also in Christ Jesus.

Reverence for Christ is the reason. Humility is the manner. The interests of the other are the aim. Submit to one another, and have the same mindset as Christ Jesus.

**Ephesians 5:21 (NIV)**
21 Submit to one another out of reverence for Christ.

**Philippians 2:1–5 (NIV)**
1 Therefore if you have any encouragement from being united with Christ, if any comfort from his love, if any common sharing in the Spirit, if any tenderness and compassion, 2 then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being one in spirit and of one mind. 3 Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. Rather, in humility value others above yourselves, 4 not looking to your own interests but each of you to the interests of the others. 5 In your relationships with one another, have the same mindset as Christ Jesus:

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has selfish ambition, or a need to be first, crowded out reverence for Christ in your house? What would it look like today to value the other above yourself, and to look to their interests?

*Scripture quotations taken from the Holy Bible, New International Version®, NIV® Copyright ©1973, 1978, 1984, 2011 by Biblica, Inc.® Used by permission. All rights reserved worldwide. lessons.body:
**Lesson 268: The marriage bed: holiness and joy**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we were called to submit to one another out of reverence for Christ, and to have his mindset in the house. Today, as we connect with this week’s Grace Life sermon, we come to the marriage bed: holiness and joy. Marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept pure, for God will judge the adulterer and all the sexually immoral. We say that with gravity and with care. Honor is not cold. Purity is not shame about the gift God has given a husband and a wife. The warning is real, and it is not a spectacle. God will judge unfaithfulness. And in the same breath, marriage is to be honored, and the bed kept pure—set apart, not treated as common, and not treated as a joke.

Proverbs speaks the same holiness as joy at home. Drink water from your own cistern, running water from your own well. Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers. May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth. The poem then calls a husband to be satisfied in his wife’s love, and not to go looking for intoxication in another. We leave the song’s own wording in the official text, and we do not linger on it as a display. The point is covenant gladness: rejoice in the wife of your youth; do not be unfaithful. Your ways are in full view of the LORD, and he examines all your paths. Lack of discipline leads to folly and death. Holiness and joy are not enemies here. The joy is at home. The holiness is the same joy kept faithful.

In *Let Marriage Be Held in Honor Among All*, on Hebrews 13:1–6, John Piper hears honor as preciousness: marriage is to be treasured, not handled casually, and the marriage bed is to be kept pure in that same honor. In *Sexual Relations in Marriage*, on Hebrews 13:4–5, he treats the bed as a place where faith itself should be at work—content, grateful, and free from the sins that defile a gift. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Proverbs 5:15–23, so that counsel is taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Proverbs: rejoice in the wife of your youth, and do not take that joy elsewhere. The BibleProject guide to Hebrews helps us hear the honor of the marriage bed in a life of love, holiness, and trust in God.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: Hebrews 13:4 has, Marriage is to be held in honor among all, and the marriage bed is to be undefiled, for the sexually immoral and adulterers God will judge. And Proverbs 5:18 has, Let your fountain be blessed, And be glad in the wife of your youth.

Honor marriage. Keep the marriage bed pure. Rejoice in the wife of your youth. Holiness and joy belong together, under the eyes of the LORD.

**Hebrews 13:4 (NIV)**
4 Marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept pure, for God will judge the adulterer and all the sexually immoral.

**Proverbs 5:15–23 (NIV)**
15 Drink water from your own cistern, running water from your own well. 16 Should your springs overflow in the streets, your streams of water in the public squares? 17 Let them be yours alone, never to be shared with strangers. 18 May your fountain be blessed, and may you rejoice in the wife of your youth. 19 A loving doe, a graceful deer— may her breasts satisfy you always, may you ever be intoxicated with her love. 20 Why, my son, be intoxicated with another man’s wife? Why embrace the bosom of a wayward woman? 21 For your ways are in full view of the LORD, and he examines all your paths. 22 The evil deeds of the wicked ensnare them; the cords of their sins hold them fast. 23 For lack of discipline they will die, led astray by their own great folly.

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, how have you been tempted to treat the marriage bed as common, as a joke, or as something less than honor? What would it look like today to keep it pure, and to rejoice, faithfully, in the one God has given you?

lessons.title: Intimacy: belonging to one another

sources.label: John Piper, Satan Uses Sexual Desire (Desiring God)

lessons.body:
**Lesson 269: Intimacy: belonging to one another**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday we heard that marriage should be honored by all, and the marriage bed kept pure, and that a husband is to rejoice in the wife of his youth. Today the same gift is named as belonging. Some in Corinth had written, “It is good for a man not to have sexual relations with a woman.” Paul does not leave that sentence standing alone. Because sexual immorality is occurring, each man should have sexual relations with his own wife, and each woman with her own husband. The husband should fulfill his marital duty to his wife, and likewise the wife to her husband. We teach this with dignity, not as a crude claim and not as a joke. Belonging here is mutual. It is a gift to be given, not a right to be seized.

The wife does not have authority over her own body but yields it to her husband. In the same way, the husband does not have authority over his own body but yields it to his wife. Do not deprive each other except perhaps by mutual consent and for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer. Then come together again so that Satan will not tempt you because of your lack of self-control. The exception is short, agreed, and aimed at prayer. The ordinary word is, do not deprive each other. Yielding is mutual. Neither spouse is a tool, and neither is left alone as if the body were only a private possession.

The Song speaks in its own reserved poetry. You have stolen my heart, my sister, my bride. How delightful is your love, my sister, my bride! The song uses the language of a garden, a spring, a sealed fountain, and an invitation, and we will not turn that language into a map or a display. The official text may be read with honor. The point we take for today is delight and belonging in the covenant: a heart stolen by one glance, a love more pleasing than wine, a garden not offered to strangers.

In *Satan Uses Sexual Desire*, on 1 Corinthians 7:1–7, John Piper takes Paul’s warning seriously, and he also takes the command as a call to give rather than to seize: each is to fulfill the other’s good, and not to refuse one another except by brief, mutual agreement for prayer. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Song of Songs 4:9–16, so the song is taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Song of Songs, which helps us hear the poem as covenant delight, not as a spectacle. The BibleProject guide to 1 Corinthians helps us keep Paul’s household word inside a letter about holiness in a careless city.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: 1 Corinthians 7:4 has, The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband does; and likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife does. **Lesson 269: Intimacy: belonging to one another**

It is a gift to be given, not a right to be seized.

Yielding is mutual. Neither spouse is a tool, and neither is left alone as if the body were only a private possession.

lessons.title: Desire, delight, and self-control

sources.label: John Piper, This Is the Will of God for You: That You Abstain from Sexual Immorality (Desiring God)

lessons.body:
**Lesson 270: Desire, delight, and self-control**

Good morning, Greg. Yesterday belonging was named as a mutual gift: do not deprive each other, and delight in the covenant. Today the Song says, I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me. There is a glad claim in that line, and a holy limit: this desire belongs inside the covenant, not outside it. The poem invites a walk to the vineyards, and says, there I will give you my love. We read the invitation with honor, and we do not turn the imagery into a show. Desire, in this book, can be spoken as delight.

Paul then names the other side of the same holiness. It is God’s will that you should be sanctified: that you should avoid sexual immorality; that each of you should learn to control your own body in a way that is holy and honorable, not in passionate lust like the pagans, who do not know God. The official range ends mid-sentence, and we do not invent a close. The word we are given is already clear: God’s will is your sanctification. Avoid sexual immorality. Learn to control your own body in a way that is holy and honorable, not in the passionate lust of people who do not know God. Delight in the covenant, and self-control, are not two religions. They are one holy life. We teach the warning with care, not as a scare, and not as a joke.

In *This Is the Will of God for You: That You Abstain from Sexual Immorality*, on 1 Thessalonians 4:1–8, John Piper takes sanctification as God’s will, not a side issue, and he ties self-control to knowing God, not merely to suppressing desire. I did not find a Piper /messages/ sermon whose main text is Song of Songs 7:10–13, so the song’s belonging and delight are taught from the text itself and from the BibleProject guide to Song of Songs. The BibleProject guide to 1 Thessalonians helps us hear holiness as the ordinary will of God for his people.

Where the LSB wording differs in a way that helps the ear: 1 Thessalonians 4:3–4 has, For this is the will of God, your sanctification: that you abstain from sexual immorality; that each of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor. And Song of Songs 7:10 has, I am my beloved’s, And his desire is for me.

I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me. That delight is covenant gladness. God’s will is your sanctification: a holy and honorable self-control, because you know God.

**Song of Songs 7:10–13 (NIV)**
10 I belong to my beloved, and his desire is for me. 11 Come, my beloved, let us go to the countryside, let us spend the night in the villages. 12 Let us go early to the vineyards to see if the vines have budded, if their blossoms have opened, and if the pomegranates are in bloom— there I will give you my love. 13 The mandrakes send out their fragrance, and at our door is every delicacy, both new and old, that I have stored up for you, my beloved.

**1 Thessalonians 4:3–5 (NIV)**
3 It is God’s will that you should be sanctified: that you should avoid sexual immorality; 4 that each of you should learn to control your own body in a way that is holy and honorable, 5 not in passionate lust like the pagans, who do not know God;

**For reflection.** As a man, husband, and father, where has desire been allowed to run like those who do not know God, or been treated as if delight had no place in a holy marriage? What would it look like today to belong, to be honorable, and to practice self-control?
